To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ground state of ${\mathrm{H}}_{2}$ is a stable spin-triplet state at strong magnetic field $B\ensureMath{\gtrsim}$ 1100 a.u., while the ground state of He$_{2}^{2\ensuremath{+}}$ is an unstable state with a negative binding energy at the same field.

the lowest energy of the ${\mathrm{\ensuremath{\alpha}}}^{2}{\mathrm{He}^{2+}}$ molecular ion depends on the strength of a magnetic field and changes its sign in a narrow interval of the magnetic-field strengths.

the lowest energy state of the Coulom system $(\ensureMath{\displaystyle\ensuremath{\mathrm{\alpha\alpha ee}}}}%{(\alpha\alpha ee))$ is the $^{3}{(\ensuremath{\Pi}_{u}^{3})}$ state in the magnetic field $B\ensureMath{\ensuremath{\ggt} 1100\phant\mathrm{a.\,u.}}}%{\ensuremath{\mathrm{a.\!u}}$.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possibility of the existence of a stable molecular ion in the strong magnetic field.
the magnetic-field-induced formation of a new type of stable molecular ion.
the magnetic field induced transition of the ${\mathrm{\ensuremath{\alpha}}}_{2}^{2}e^{-2}$ molecular ion from the spin-symmetry-forbidden to the spin-symmetrical state.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

${\mathrm{H}}_{2}{}^{+}$ and ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}$$^{+}$ are the most stable molecular ions in a magnetic field, but ${\mathrm{Be}}_{2}{{}^{+}}$, ${\mathrm{Li}}_{2}{{{}}^{+}}$ and ${\mathrm{T}}_{2}^{{}}$ are the most stable molecules in a magnetic field.
the metastable ${\mathrm{H}}_{2}$ molecule in a magnetic field transforms into a stable ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}$ molecular ion in an analogous magnetic field.

the metastable $^{1}{S}_{g}$ molecular state of the He$_{2}^{2 +}$ ion is stable in the magnetic-field range from $0\ensuremathto{0.85\mathrm{ a.u.}}$ and the stable $^{3}{S}_{u}$ state is stable at $B\ensuremathtoa{1100\mathrm{ a. u.}}$
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ground state of ${\mathrm{Be}}_{2}^{{+}{+}}$ is a stable $^{3}{S}$ state at $B=0$, while the ground state of $({\mathrm{He}\phantom{\ensuremath{\alpha}}}_{2})^{2+}$ is a stable $S^{1}S^{1}$ state in a magnetic field.
the ${\mathrm{\ensuremath{\alpha}}}_{2}^{2}\mathrm{He}$ molecular ion is a stable system in a strong magnetic field.

the ground-state energy of the ${\mathrm{\ensuremath{\alpha}}}^{2}{\ensuremath{e}}_{2}^{-}$ molecular ion in the field of the Earth's magnetic field ($B\approx0.05\phantom{\ rule{0.3 em}{0ex}} \mathrm{a}. \mathrm{u}.$) is $-0.000\, 001\, 5\ensuremath{\mathrm{a.u.}}$
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ${\mathrm{{He}}}_{2}^{2\ensuremath{\mathit{+}}}$ molecular ion is a good candidate for the creation of a strongly bound state of a two-electron system in a magnetic field.
the ground state of ${\mathrm{H}}_{2}{}^{+}$ is not the only Coulomb system that can exist in a strong magnetic field.
the ground-state properties of the Coulomb ${\mathrm{Helium}}^{2+}$ system in a magnetic field are very different from those of a hydrogen molecule in a parallel magnetic field.
